headline: High: ChatGPT Desktop can read user files/screenshots while social-auto-upload can exfiltrate media to broad-network platforms, creating dangerous default leakage and action-cascade risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can ingest files, screenshots, clipboard, and supported-app content by default, while social-auto-upload handles media files and account data. If B’s uploaded captions or metadata are later copied into A, malicious instructions could ride the shared content path. The bridge is indirect, but the shared file/media workflow makes injection plausible.
conditions: IF outputs from social-auto-upload are copied into ChatGPT Desktop via clipboard or files
IF ChatGPT Desktop is asked to interpret uploaded media captions or account text as instructions
mitigations: Use a strict delimiter/template for copied text
Strip instructions from captions before transfer
Review B outputs in plain text before pasting into A
Disable clipboard bridging during review sessions
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between tools

B_data_leakage.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-IDE code, while social-auto-upload has broad network egress and handles account data plus media files. If A’s sensitive inputs are forwarded into B for posting or automation, B can transmit them externally. The pair creates a realistic exfiltration path in default workflows.
conditions: IF ChatGPT Desktop receives sensitive uploaded files or screenshots
IF social-auto-upload is used on content derived from A’s outputs or connected IDE code
mitigations: Do not pass sensitive A outputs into B
Redact screenshots and files before transfer
Use a staging folder with non-sensitive test media
Restrict B to a separate account with dummy data
requires-engineering: enforce DLP between A and B

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Neither agent writes the filesystem or modifies git state, so direct write-write conflict is absent. ChatGPT Desktop can read files and social-auto-upload can operate on account/media files, but the overlap is mostly read/transfer rather than concurrent mutation. The pair is therefore low risk for capability conflict.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable directory through an external orchestrator
IF an operator manually copies files between the two during the same task
mitigations: Keep separate working directories
Avoid concurrent edits to shared assets
Use read-only mounts for A
Use a staging copy for B uploads

D_cascading_error.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can generate content from files and screenshots, and social-auto-upload is explicitly an uploader/automation tool with broad network egress. If B treats A’s generated captions, summaries, or instructions as authoritative, errors can cascade into public posts or account actions. That downstream action authority makes the blast radius high.
conditions: IF B uses A-generated text as the source of truth for uploads
IF A’s output is not manually verified before posting
mitigations: Require human review before upload
Compare A output against source media
Use a draft-only posting mode
Limit B to test accounts first
requires-engineering: add verification gates before publish

E_compliance.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop processes uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-IDE code, while social-auto-upload handles account data and media with broad network egress. If regulated or personal data is moved from A into B for posting, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF personal or regulated data from A is forwarded into B
IF B posts or stores content under a different retention policy than A
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B workflows
Use synthetic test content
Document retention for both tools
Review account-region settings before posting
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls
